questions.stem: Which skin area does an adductor canal block mainly cover?
options: Skin of the lateral thigh and hip
Skin of the medial leg and foot
Skin of the lateral leg and dorsum of foot

questions.stem: A large subsartorial volume in an adductor canal block can partly block which muscle?
An adductor canal block added to a sciatic block is used for which surgery?
Which procedure is an adductor canal block indicated for?
In knee surgery, what role does an adductor canal block play?
questions.answer: Analgesia, as part of multimodal analgesia

questions.stem: Where does the adductor canal run?
options: From the inguinal ligament to the knee
From the apex of the femoral triangle to the adductor hiatus
From the adductor hiatus to the popliteal fossa
From the femoral crease to the patella

questions.stem: Where is the apex of the femoral triangle?
questions.answer: Where the medial border of sartorius crosses the medial border of adductor longus

questions.stem: What is the adductor hiatus?
questions.answer: Where the superficial femoral vessels dive deep towards the popliteal fossa, away from sartorius

questions.stem: An injection in the aponeurotic compartment proximal to the femoral triangle apex is by definition which block?
Under the subcutaneous fat, what shape does the adductor canal have?
Which muscle forms the lateral wall of the adductor canal?
In an ultrasound adductor canal block, where is the saphenous nerve usually found?
In the adductor canal, which vein runs with the femoral artery and nerve?
Near the knee, what artery lies close to the saphenous nerve in an adductor canal block?
questions.answer: Descending genicular artery and its saphenous branch

questions.stem: An ultrasound-guided adductor canal block uses a ____ transducer.
What needle length is used for an ultrasound-guided adductor canal block?
What local anaesthetic volume is typical for an ultrasound adductor canal block?
Which volume is linked to possible partial quadriceps weakness in an adductor canal block?
For an adductor canal block, how proximal should the injection be placed?
For an ultrasound adductor canal block, how is the thigh positioned to expose the medial thigh?
questions.answer: Abducted and externally rotated, with the patient supine

questions.stem: In an ultrasound adductor canal block, how deep is the femoral artery usually found?
If the nerve is poorly seen, where should local anaesthetic go in an adductor canal block?
questions.answer: Next to the artery, in the plane between sartorius and vastus medialis

questions.stem: What test volume confirms position in an ultrasound adductor canal block?
If the needle tip is not visible in an adductor canal block, what bolus size is used while advancing?
What success rate is reported for the transsartorial landmark adductor canal approach?
In the transsartorial landmark adductor canal approach, what is the patient position?
In the transsartorial approach, how is the sartorius located just above the knee?
questions.answer: Feel for it with the leg straight and actively lifted

questions.stem: In the transsartorial approach, where is the needle inserted?
questions.answer: One finger-width above the patella, over the sartorius belly

questions.stem: In the transsartorial approach, what needle direction is aimed for through the muscle?
questions.answer: Slightly posterior to the coronal plane and slightly caudad

questions.stem: In the transsartorial approach, how deep is loss of resistance typically found?
In the transsartorial approach, what volume is injected after aspiration?
